title: George Williams, Barney Gilbert and other Navy bandsmen
summary: More Navy band members: George Williams, Barney Gilbert, Herbert Leary; what they played; most were from New Orleans.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Did you know George Williams
from, uh... Yeah, George Williams. He come from Downersonville. George was, uh... George was, uh... head, uh... band man down there.
Yeah.
And little Barney Gilbert was down there, too. You know him?
No, who is he?
Oh, he's a trumpet player, too.
Oh, Vernon Gilbert.
Yeah, Barney Gilbert.
Yeah, he's kin to John Casimir, too, I think.
No, I don't believe he's no kin to John. He used to play
with John, though.

He's a mailman. That's right. He used to play with John. The mailman. That's right. He used to play with John. Yeah. That's a long time. Well, he was down in the Navy band. Practically, most of the fellows in that Navy band was right out of New Orleans. Outside George Williams, which was there, but from Dyson Root. And, uh... two trombone players. I didn't know them. They wasn't... they wasn't from here. So...
What did George Williams play?
Uh...
What did George Williams play?
George Williams? George Williams used to play trumpet and sax.
And, uh, Herbert Leary, what was he playing then?
Who that?
Leary.
He played trumpet. Yeah, he played trumpet. Yeah.
Was that his main instrument? Trumpet? Was trumpet his main instrument?
Was that his main goal? That's what he played down there.
At the Navy?
Yeah. Oh, Gilbert Young was a nice trumpet player himself.
He played beautiful breaks. You don't hear many trumpet players that play good, clean breaks anymore. Yeah.
